voices.note: תנו רבנן (57b.20): the anonymous first tanna of the baraita on Mercury and on a place from which idolatry was uprooted
disputes the baraita's outside-the-Land exemption, within the same baraita

props.gloss_en: one who sees Mercury says: 'Blessed... Who has given patience to those who transgress His will'

[one who sees] a place from which idolatry was uprooted says: 'Blessed... Who uprooted idolatry from our land; and as it was uprooted from this place, so may it be uprooted from all the places of Israel, and turn the heart of their worshippers to worship You'
outside the Land one need not say 'and turn the heart of their worshippers to worship You'
because its [the land outside Israel's] majority is gentiles
R' Shimon ben Elazar: even outside the Land one must say so
because they are destined to convert
as it is said: 'for then I will turn to the peoples a pure language' (Zeph 3:9)
